headline: Applied Materials has opened a research centre in California where TSMC, Intel, Samsung, Micron and SK hynix will develop future AI chip technology alongside its engineers.
score_reason: Pool 7 lowered by 1: the opening was announced on 12 Oct, before the window, and earlier partner news was already in our 1 Oct and 7 Oct editions.
importance_line: If the shared-lab model works, new chip-making methods could reach factories sooner, which matters to everyone who depends on AI hardware and to the rival chipmakers now working side by side, but the speed-up is a stated goal and the $5 billion is spending expected over time, not money already spent.
summary: CTech reports that Applied Materials, a US maker of chip-manufacturing equipment, has opened its EPIC Center in Sunnyvale, California, a research site where TSMC, Intel, Samsung, Micron and SK hynix will work beside its engineers and university researchers on future chip technology; the company announced the opening on 12 Oct 2026, after Kioxia (our 1 Oct edition) and Intel (our 7 Oct edition) had announced projects there. Applied Materials expects its spending on the centre to grow to about $5 billion over time as customer projects begin, and the promised faster route to mass production is a goal that has not yet been shown.
notes: Opening announced 12 Oct (Evertiq, Financial-News.co.uk), before the window; score lowered by 1 as instructed. Not in the 13 Oct pool titles. The CTech page text was read from the article data in the page source.
